newsitem.title: USA: US FCC seeks to reform formal complaint process.
newsitem.headline: US FCC seeks to reform formal complaint process.

text.p: To speed the deregulation of the telecommunications industry, the Federal Communications Commission Tuesday proposed to streamline its process for settling complaints by phone carriers against one another.
The new communications law prescribed deadlines ranging from 90 days to five months for the FCC to resolve certain complaints against the Baby Bell phone companies and other carriers.

The FCC went a step further and proposed to apply its proposal to all formal complaints filed with the agency. Formal complaints refer to those involving carriers, as opposed to consumer complaints. Up to now, disputes could take up to a year or so to be settled.
The FCC wants to encourage parties to narrow the issues involved in any dispute. The FCC also wants to develop methods for improving the quality and content of parties' filings.
The number of complaints is expected to grow as the FCC seeks to open local phone markets to competition and consider the entry of the Baby Bells into the long-distance market.
"I expect the volume of complaints will increase substantially over the coming months," said Commissioner Susan Ness.
